name: NY-22
label: Safe D

Incumbent John Mannion has a large financial edge, with $1.8 million on hand versus under $200,000 for Kailee Buller

model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Mannion: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly ten-to-one cash advantage over Buller, with markets pricing the race near 94% Democratic. With no polls to contradict that picture, the forecast stays safely Democratic with a modest haircut to the baseline margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race, or heavy outside spending against Mannion, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-22 is a central New York House district that leans Democratic by about four points, and first-term incumbent John Mannion is seeking reelection. He has raised $2.7 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Kailee Buller has raised about $267,000 with under $200,000 available. No outside groups are active on either side, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Mannion's chances around 94%. With no public polling available, the forecast relies on fundamentals: the district lean, incumbency, a favorable spending environment, and the large financial gap all point to a comfortable Democratic win, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
